events.title: Nicolaus Copernicus dies in Frombork
events.description: Copernicus died weeks after his On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres was printed; tradition says he saw a copy on his deathbed. His Sun-centred model began a revolution in astronomy.
events.html: Copernicus died weeks after his On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres was printed; tradition says he saw a copy on his deathbed. His Sun-centred model began a revolution in astronomy.

events.title: Toleration Act grants freedom of worship to Dissenters
events.description: The Act allowed Protestant Nonconformists in England to worship in their own licensed meeting houses. Catholics and anti-Trinitarians were excluded.
events.html: The Act allowed Protestant Nonconformists in England to worship in their own licensed meeting houses. Catholics and anti-Trinitarians were excluded.

events.title: John Wesley feels his heart 'strangely warmed'
events.description: At a meeting in Aldersgate Street, London, John Wesley experienced an assurance of faith while hearing Luther's preface to Romans read. The experience energised the Methodist movement.
events.html: At a meeting in Aldersgate Street, London, John Wesley experienced an assurance of faith while hearing Luther's preface to Romans read. The experience energised the Methodist movement.

events.title: Samuel Morse sends 'What hath God wrought'
events.description: Morse tapped out the biblical phrase from the Capitol in Washington to Alfred Vail in Baltimore. The line opened the age of the electric telegraph in the United States.
events.html: Morse tapped out the biblical phrase from the Capitol in Washington to Alfred Vail in Baltimore. The line opened the age of the electric telegraph in the United States.

events.title: Brooklyn Bridge opens across the East River
events.description: After fourteen years of construction, the bridge linking Manhattan and Brooklyn opened. It was then the longest suspension bridge in the world, the first to use steel wire cables.
events.html: After fourteen years of construction, the bridge linking Manhattan and Brooklyn opened. It was then the longest suspension bridge in the world, the first to use steel wire cables.

events.title: Bismarck sinks HMS Hood in the Denmark Strait
events.description: A shell from the German battleship detonated Hood's magazine, and she sank in minutes; only three of her 1,418 crew survived. The Royal Navy hunted Bismarck down three days later.
events.html: A shell from the German battleship detonated Hood's magazine, and she sank in minutes; only three of her 1,418 crew survived. The Royal Navy hunted Bismarck down three days later.
